sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Zanesville, Ohio?
sections.html:
Zanesville is the Muskingum County seat, built where the Licking River meets the Muskingum River about 52 miles east of Columbus. The 2025 Census estimate of 25,138 people is a 1.4% rise over the 24,783 in the 2020 estimates base, which follows decades of loss from a 1950 peak of 40,517.

The city is named for Ebenezer Zane, whose pioneer trail crossed the Muskingum here, and it served as Ohio's second state capital from 1810 to 1812. The National Road, now U.S. 40, runs through town alongside Interstate 70, and U.S. 22 and state routes 60 and 93 also pass through. The three-way Y-Bridge over the river junction is on the National Register of Historic Places.

Zanesville was once known for pottery. Weller, Roseville and J. B. Owens operated here in the first half of the twentieth century, drawing on local clay deposits. The city peaked economically in the 1950s, and Wikipedia describes its present economy as having relatively high poverty and low labor force participation.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about the Zanesville housing market?
sections.html:
Renters outnumber owners here. QuickFacts reports 43.8% owner occupancy for 2020 to 2024, the lowest of the four cities, alongside a $123,700 median home value and $821 median gross rent.

  • There are 10,601 households averaging 2.28 people.
  • Households earn a median $43,280, and 24.1% of residents live below the poverty line.
  • Bachelor's degrees reach 15.1% of adults, and 85.4% finished high school.
  • Commutes average 22.8 minutes each way.
  • Health care and social assistance took in about $1.01 billion in 2022, and retailers sold about $907 million, which works out to $36,876 per resident, the top figure of the four.

With fewer than half of homes occupied by owners, tenants are part of many sales. If your house has a tenant, tell buyers whether the lease runs past closing and who holds the deposit.

sections.h2: Which schools, colleges and hospitals serve Zanesville?
sections.html:
Most students inside the city limits attend Zanesville City Schools, with Zanesville High School as the high school. A few northern pockets of the city belong to the West Muskingum and Tri-Valley local districts, so check which district serves your parcel before advertising it. Private options include Bishop Rosecrans High School and Zanesville Christian School.

Higher education is local. Ohio University Zanesville is a branch campus of Ohio University, and Zane State College sits next to it. Muskingum University is in nearby New Concord. In 2016 the Good Samaritan and Bethesda campuses merged to form Genesis Hospital, and Good Samaritan was closed and demolished.

sections.h2: How does Zanesville's building and code enforcement office affect a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Building and Code Enforcement office, at 401 Market Street, Room 227, enforces the International Property Maintenance Code, the city's codified ordinances and the zoning code, and it can start legal proceedings against violators. Weekday hours run 7:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 740-617-4890.

The office also issues and inspects the permits a buyer's inspector will ask about:

  • Residential building, electrical and mechanical permits, which do not include plumbing.
  • Residential and commercial sidewalk, curb and curb cut permits.
  • Demolition permits.
  • Permits to move a house or an accessory structure wider than 14 feet or larger than 450 square feet.
  • Certificates of occupancy.

The office keeps lists of condemned properties and posts a 2026 annual vacant property form among its code enforcement forms. If your house is vacant, ask the office whether the form applies before you list it. For zoning questions, the county auditor's page lists the city's Planning and Zoning office at 740-617-4909. South Zanesville has its own permit department at 740-454-0492, which matters if your address is just outside the city line.

sections.h2: How do Muskingum County values, appeals and homestead rules work?
sections.html:
The Muskingum County Auditor works from the courthouse at 401 Main Street, takes calls at (740) 455-7109 and keeps weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. The auditor explains that the January 2026 tax bills reflect values set in January 2025, and that an addition, a demolition or newly passed levies can change a bill.

A three-member Board of Revision (auditor, treasurer and commissioners' president, or their designees) adjusts values and has no say over tax dollars. A complaint is a legal filing, lodged with the auditor from January 1 to March 31. The auditor's page warns that a filing is generally limited to once per three years and that withdrawing one uses up the turn. Points that help a seller:

  • Proof is on you, and the outcome can be a higher value, a lower one or none at all.
  • Certified mail brings the hearing notice at least ten days before the date.
  • After a filing, an appraiser from the auditor may visit and propose a settlement figure. Accepting it in writing cancels the hearing.
  • A corporation should have an attorney file for it.

The auditor's brochure for tax year 2025 explains the Homestead Exemption for seniors, disabled owners and surviving spouses. It prints a $29,000 reduction in taxable market value, an income limit of $41,000 that is adjusted annually for inflation, a December 31 filing deadline, and a larger reduction for disabled veterans equal to the tax on up to $58,000 of market value. A seller who receives the exemption should ask the auditor how a sale affects it on that parcel.

sections.h2: What must a Zanesville seller tell the buyer?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 puts a state form in the hands of every one to four unit seller. Fill it in honestly and deliver it promptly. A seller is not liable for an inaccuracy that was outside the seller's actual knowledge, though a buyer given the form late can walk away within three business days.

Gather permit numbers and any notices from the code office before showings, so the buyer sees them with the form.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense for a Zanesville house?
sections.html:
Consider a cash offer for a rental with tenant trouble, an inherited house or a place whose repairs would worry a lender's appraiser. It can also end the monthly cost of a vacant house that keeps drawing taxes and utility bills.

Collect more than one written offer, compare closing costs and closing dates, and ask the title company for the settlement statement a day or two before you sign.

faqs.q: Who do I call about zoning in Zanesville?
faqs.a: Phone the city's Planning and Zoning office at 740-617-4909. The county auditor's zoning page lists that number next to separate contacts for South Zanesville and several townships, since zoning follows the address.

faqs.q: How often can I appeal my Muskingum County property value?
faqs.a: Once in each three-year period, as a rule. The auditor receives complaints from January 1 until March 31, and one that is later withdrawn still counts as your filing.

faqs.q: Can the Board of Revision raise my value?
faqs.a: Yes, the auditor's page says the board may go up, go down or leave the number alone, and that the burden is on the owner. Bring a recent sale, an appraisal or repair estimates.

faqs.q: Does a vacant Zanesville house need to be registered?
faqs.a: The city's code enforcement page carries an annual vacant property form for 2026. Phone 740-617-4890 to learn whether your address must file before a sale.

faqs.q: What permits might a buyer ask me about in Zanesville?
faqs.a: A buyer's inspector may ask about residential building, electrical and mechanical permits, demolition permits and certificates of occupancy, all issued by the city's Building and Code Enforcement office. Bring permit numbers for any addition or major system replacement.
